messages:
PD Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered: INC-23987 — service=redwood-runtime-prod. Alert routed to schedule 'core-infra-schedule' (expected: runtime-oncall). https://pagerduty.example/incidents/INC-23987

Amy Chen: wait — why is runtime-prod going to core-infra? that’s not our routing rule.

Josh Patel: I just got woken up by PD. I'm not on runtime rotation. Looks like the schedule mapping changed during the weekly sync.

Kevin Liu: I’m seeing the same. PD incident shows escalation policy = core-infra-escalation. That’s wrong.

Lia Gomez: Confirming: recent schedule import job (ci/pd-sync) pushed a mapping that points runtime-prod -> core-infra-schedule. Probably a YAML key mismatch.

Marta Rivera: Paging chain started, two engineers acked before it escalated. Customer-facing errors spiked: 503s on model inference for ~12min.

Carla Soto: Support just logged 6 customer tickets referencing time window 06:14–06:30 UTC. Severity?

Amy Chen: marking severity P2 for now, because some customers impacted but mitigation available.

Josh Patel: I suppressed the route temporarily in PD (manual suppress) to stop further wakeups. 

Oncall Bot: Incident INC-23987 acknowledged by Josh Patel. Escalation halted.

Kevin Liu: Root cause short: schedule import script used an old mapping file. It overwrote the runtime service routing with core-infra-schedule because of a duplicate key in the sync YAML.

Lia Gomez: Immediate mitigations taken:
- suppressed PD notifications for INC-23987
- created temporary override routing rule: runtime-prod -> runtime-oncall (manual)
- set CI job to paused for PD sync until patch review

Amy Chen: Commands I ran to reroute (for the record):
```
pd-ctl routes update --service redwood-runtime-prod --escalation runtime-oncall --reason "temporary reroute after bad sync"
pd-ctl incident suppress INC-23987 --until 2026-11-01T07:00:00Z
```

Josh Patel: After reroute, I manually paged runtime-oncall to confirm they saw it; they acknowledged and started mitigation on the app side.

Marta Rivera: Customer impact tally (initial): 6 tickets open, error-rate bump 503 +1200% at peak, estimated affected requests ~3.4k. I'll update support dashboard.

Carla Soto: Notifying affected customers with a short statement now — will include ETA and a pointer to status.redwood.ai.

Kevin Liu: Postfix actions we need:
1) Fix the CI sync to validate for duplicate keys and schema (owner: Kevin)
2) Add a PD integration test that verifies service->schedule mapping after deploy (owner: Amy)
3) Run a manual audit of critical services mappings (owner: Josh)
4) Update runbook to include manual reroute steps and `pd-ctl` snippet (owner: Lia)

Amy Chen: I'll schedule a short post-incident run at 13:00 UTC to walk through timeline and confirm PD test coverage.

Josh Patel: Quick note: the schedule change occurred during a small on-call rotation update yesterday; the sync job uses a different key name in the new file and the validator didn't catch it. We'll add stricter diffs.

Oncall Bot: Incident INC-23987 status -> mitigated.

Marta Rivera: Support: updating customers with incident summary, marking updates on status page.

Carla Soto: +1 on the post-incident call. Can we include SRE, Platform, Support?

Amy Chen: Yes. Calendar invite sent to SRE, Platform, Support, PD owners. Postmortem doc draft in google: https://docs.google.com/document/d/incident-23987-draft

Kevin Liu: I'll open a PR to add YAML schema check and a smoke test that the PD mapping is correct. Reference for reviewers: repo infra/ci-pd-sync (branch: pd-fix/validate-mapping).

Josh Patel: Also adding an alert to detect high rate of manual suppressions for the same service — that should cut down on repeated noisy wakeups.

Marta Rivera: Final customer impact note for tickets: affected timeframe 06:14–06:30 UTC, degraded inference (errors 503). No data exposure.

Amy Chen: Closing this thread. Follow-up actions in the postmortem doc and PRs assigned. Thanks everyone for fast responses. :thumbsup:
